correctness.rationale: From a standard one-dimensional Brownian hitting density f(s)=e^{-1/(4s)}/(2√πs^(3/2)), independent exponential mortality and Poisson recruitment give exact P(τ>t0s)=(1−F_m(s))e^(−ρmJ_m(s)) with m=x logρ. A reciprocal-endpoint substitution w=1/(4s) gives F_m~e^(−w−m/(4w))/√(πw), J_m~e^(−w−m/(4w))/(4√π w^(5/2)) uniformly w=L+O(logL), x bounded away from zero and infinity. With centering C_L=L−1.5logL+log(x/(4√π))−x/4, ρmJ_m→e^(−z), producing standard Gumbel. Analytical tail bounds at w≈L/2 and dominated kernels control all fixed integer moments, permit E[1/(4(C_L+G_L))] expansion and the displayed second-order mean term; x/4−log x has unique fixed-positive-x minimum at x=4. Independently checked the endpoint intensity at L=50 and L=150 for x=1,4,8 and z=−1,0,1; errors decrease but finite convergence is slow. No finite-ρ global minimizer claimed.
